description: A U+FEFF at the start of an object expression's property name is dropped
notes: The spec says a string is a standalone template, whose literal text can hold any character except the sequences that start interpolations and directives, which keeps U+FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE. The native syntax spec also says byte order marks aren't permitted in source, which read as applying to a template's text would make this an error; neither reading drops the character. hashicorp/hcl parses the string with the native template parser ((*expression).Value in json/structure.go), which removes a leading byte order mark from any source it scans (stripUTF8BOM in hclsyntax/token.go), also for property names, which are templates too.
